{"id": "33:5/q03", "question": "What happened around the verse's revelation?", "turns_on": "Reports vary in persons named and narrative detail.", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q03/p1", "position": "Zayd was called Muhammad's son until the verse restored his father's name.", "reasons": "Ibn Umar's report is noted as transmitted by Bukhari; Durr and Alusi give Haritha ibn Shurahbil or Sharahil. Muqatil says Zayd affirmed his known descent. Tirmidhi grades Aisha's longer narrative gharīb and notes a shorter route through Masruq."}, {"id": "33:5/q03/p2", "position": "Zayd's adoption and the Prophet's marriage to Zaynab prompted accusations that he married his son's former wife.", "reasons": "Thaʿlabi and Wahidi name Jews and hypocrites; Ibn Kathir links 33:37 and says 4:23 concerns sons from one's loins."}, {"id": "33:5/q03/p3", "position": "Zayd was captured and sold, passed through Khadija to Muhammad, then chose Muhammad over his birth family.", "reasons": "Qurtubi places capture in Syria and describes the ransom party; Durr names Ukaz as the sale place; Alusi and Kuranyolu recount his emancipation and adoption."}, {"id": "33:5/q03/p4", "position": "The verse concerned Zayd, Salim, Amir ibn Rabi'a and al-Miqdad.", "reasons": "Durr transmits al-Hasan ibn Uthman's report."}, {"id": "33:5/q03/p5", "position": "Salim was adopted by Abu Hudhayfa and treated as a son and heir until the verse.", "reasons": "Aisha or Urwa reports the old inheritance custom; Nasai says Abu Hudhayfa arranged Salim's marriage; Bursevi says he later bore a client name. Ibn Atiyya says people cited both Zayd and Salim as adoptively named."}, {"id": "33:5/q03/p6", "position": "Al-Miqdad, Sufyan and Salim show correction or persistence of earlier affiliation.", "reasons": "Mawardi gives their distinct lineages; Qurtubi observes continuing names; Ibn Ashur disputes inferring deliberate intent from old usage."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q04", "question": "What legal effects can adoption or a sonship claim have?", "turns_on": "Adoption alone versus a possible claim of paternity, and its effect on an enslaved person.", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q04/p1", "position": "Adoption itself creates no biological lineage, inheritance, or mahram status.", "reasons": "Qurtubi and Nasafi describe the older inheritance custom; Ibn Ashur limits an express bequest to one-third; Kuranyolu lists marriage, covering, rights and duties, while citing a Prophetic reward for orphan care."}, {"id": "33:5/q04/p2", "position": "A plausible paternity claim for a younger person of unknown lineage establishes filiation and emancipates that person if enslaved.", "reasons": "Abu Hanifa's view appears in Jishumi, Baydawi, Nasafi, Bursevi, Ibn Ashur and Alusi. Jishumi presumes truthful conformity to the marital bed."}, {"id": "33:5/q04/p3", "position": "An impossible paternity claim establishes no lineage but, for Abu Hanifa, frees an enslaved person.", "reasons": "Known lineage or older age blocks filiation; Bursevi contrasts denial of an adoptee with denial of a biological child, liʿan and hadd."}, {"id": "33:5/q04/p4", "position": "An impossible claim is void and does not free an enslaved person.", "reasons": "Bursevi and Ibn Ashur attribute this to Abu Hanifa's two companions."}, {"id": "33:5/q04/p5", "position": "Adoption has no legal effect, including no emancipation.", "reasons": "Baydawi gives his school view; Alusi attributes it to Shafiʿi."}, {"id": "33:5/q04/p6", "position": "The verse distinguishes error and intent in lineage rulings.", "reasons": "Jishumi draws this legal inference."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q05", "question": "On what basis is lineage established?", "turns_on": "Marital bed versus presumption and proof.", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q05/p1", "position": "The established marital bed grounds lineage.", "reasons": "Jishumi offers this answer and Tabarsi mentions men whose marital beds children were born in."}, {"id": "33:5/q05/p2", "position": "Presumption governs unless truthful report, evidence or necessity establishes descent.", "reasons": "Jishumi cites the necessarily known descent to Adnan and many Companions' lineages."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q06", "question": "What does 'more just before God' mean?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q06/p1", "position": "True paternal naming is more just, true and correct than false adoptive lineage.", "reasons": "Muqatil, Qatada and Zajjaj gloss aqsaṭ as more just; Mawardi adds just in speech and judgment; Ibn Ashur says the contrary erases fathers' and adoptees' rights. Bursevi cites Kashf al-asrar for greater justice and truthfulness."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q07", "question": "What does 'it' refer to?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q07/p1", "position": "The verbal noun implied by the command: calling them by their fathers' names.", "reasons": "Samin, Alusi and Tabatabai compare 5:8; Baydawi and Ibn Ashur identify the naming act."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q08", "question": "Is aqsaṭ an absolute or a comparative expression?", "turns_on": "Full justice versus explicit comparison with prior adoptive naming.", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q08/p1", "position": "It expresses full or absolute justice.", "reasons": "Razi compares 'God is greater'; Alusi derives it from qisṭ; Ibn Ashur says the false alternative is no justice."}, {"id": "33:5/q08/p2", "position": "It compares true attribution with the prior false name.", "reasons": "Razi supplies the old practice as comparator; Alusi calls the comparison ironic."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q09", "question": "Why state that paternal naming is more just?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q09/p1", "position": "It justifies the command and reassures those attached to the old custom.", "reasons": "Ibn Ashur calls it explanatory resumption linked to 33:4; Baydawi connects the prior 'statements of truth'; Biqai says it prepares later events."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q10", "question": "What if an adoptee's father is unknown?", "turns_on": "Whether the fallback is religious brotherhood, clientage, or both according to status.", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q10/p1", "position": "Do not invent adoptive lineage; treat the person as a brother in faith and, when applicable, a client or ally.", "reasons": "Tabari excludes the adopter; Mawardi distinguishes free brothers and freed clients; Ibn Ashur says either designation preserves closeness. Mawardi reports Salman naming himself son of Islam and Umar affirming it. Zajjaj says to call a believing unknown-father person brother."}, {"id": "33:5/q10/p2", "position": "Use a conventional patronal name such as son of Abdullah or Abd al-Rahman.", "reasons": "Farra and Muqatil ibn Hayyan give examples; Durr reports Muqatil on brother and patron names."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q11", "question": "How does 'if you do not know' work grammatically?", "turns_on": "Past-negating lam under a conditional.", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q11/p1", "position": "It means not knowing or recognizing the fathers, so paternal attribution is unavailable.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Jawzi and Alusi explain this."}, {"id": "33:5/q11/p2", "position": "In can be understood as idh, a past-time particle.", "reasons": "Bursevi reports this analysis for an impossible condition."}, {"id": "33:5/q11/p3", "position": "Lam turns the present verb into a past form the conditional governs.", "reasons": "Bursevi reports Baydawi's explanation and cites 2:24."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q12", "question": "What is the syntax of 'your brothers and clients'?", "turns_on": "Nominative predicates or accusatives under an omitted imperative.", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q12/p1", "position": "They are nominative predicates of an omitted 'they'.", "reasons": "Farra says an implied 'they are' licenses this; Ibn al-Jawzi and Ibn Ashur supply the subject; Nahhas coordinates mawālī with ikhwa."}, {"id": "33:5/q12/p2", "position": "They may be accusative under an implicit 'call them'.", "reasons": "Farra contrasts cases continuing an earlier verb and gives examples of food and clothing."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q13", "question": "What does 'in religion' convey?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q13/p1", "position": "Brotherhood belongs to or is caused by their shared faith.", "reasons": "Majaz says religious community; Tabari compares 9:11; Ibn Ashur gives figurative containment or cause, citing 29:10 and 49:10."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q14", "question": "Who are the mawālī here?", "turns_on": "Freed clients, paternal cousins, or allies.", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q14/p1", "position": "Freed clients of emancipators.", "reasons": "Al-Suddi and Muqatil use freedmen; Wahidi cites Zayd; Tabarsi says their walā belongs to emancipators; Salim illustrates this."}, {"id": "33:5/q14/p2", "position": "Paternal cousins.", "reasons": "Majaz gives this alongside patrons; Wahidi cites Ibn Abbas, Mubarrad and Zajjaj with a poetic line; Tabarsi accepts it."}, {"id": "33:5/q14/p3", "position": "Allies or protectors in religion or by pact.", "reasons": "Zajjaj says religious allies; Tabarsi mentions mutual support; Ibn Ashur says pact allies specifically rather than freedmen."}, {"id": "33:5/q14/p4", "position": "A broad relationship term including heirs, Master, protector and friend.", "reasons": "Study Quran cites 4:33, 19:5, 2:286, 3:150, 6:62 and 8:40 and notes its relation to walī."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q15", "question": "May one call a sinner 'my brother' or 'my client'?", "turns_on": "Whether the honorific is restricted for a sinner.", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q15/p1", "position": "The two forms of address are equally permitted, perhaps subject to the person not being sinful.", "reasons": "Alusi suggests this qualification."}, {"id": "33:5/q15/p2", "position": "Calling a sinner 'my client' is forbidden where it honors him; the same reason could cover 'brother'.", "reasons": "Alusi reports a hadith-based or honor-based restriction."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q16", "question": "What does 'no blame for what you erred in' cover?", "turns_on": "Earlier custom, mistaken belief, slips

, or a general rule; Ibn Atiyya and Abu Hayyan reject calling lawful prior conduct error.", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q16/p1", "position": "Earlier adoption and misnaming before prohibition are pardoned.", "reasons": "Mujahid contrasts before and after clarification; Study Quran says adopters then had no intent to oppose God."}, {"id": "33:5/q16/p2", "position": "Honest error about who a father is is excused, even after inquiry.", "reasons": "Qatada supplies the believed-father case; Ibn Kathir cites 2:286, God's answer in Muslim, and the mistaken judge's reward."}, {"id": "33:5/q16/p3", "position": "Forgetfulness, habitual slips, and affectionate nonliteral address are excused.", "reasons": "Yahya applies it after prohibition; Habib emphasizes forgetfulness; Razi likens it to inadvertent oath; Ibn Ashur rejects inferring intent from a persistent old name."}, {"id": "33:5/q16/p4", "position": "The negation establishes a broad exemption for mistakes, forgetfulness and compulsion.", "reasons": "Nahhas and Qurtubi give mistaken payment and greeting under oaths; Ibn Kathir, Alusi, Ibn Ashur and Study Quran cite the Prophetic lifting of three things, with 2:286; Biqai includes zihar."}, {"id": "33:5/q16/p5", "position": "The exemption is specific to adoptive attribution.", "reasons": "Alusi offers this as the narrower reading."}, {"id": "33:5/q16/p6", "position": "Conduct before a prohibition is not properly called an error.", "reasons": "Ibn Atiyya defines khataʾ as deviation and distinguishes knowing khāṭiʾ from unaware mukhtiʾ, citing 69:37; Abu Hayyan agrees."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q17", "question": "What does junāḥ mean and where might it come from?", "turns_on": "Arabic derivation versus a proposed Persian loan.", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q17/p1", "position": "It means sin, linked to inclining from truth.", "reasons": "Bursevi compares a listing ship; Ibn Ashur uses the sense to infer obligation."}, {"id": "33:5/q17/p2", "position": "It may derive from Persian gunāh.", "reasons": "Bursevi reports sound substitutions and compares jawhar from gohar."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q18", "question": "What does akhta'tum imply in form and usage?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q18/p1", "position": "It indicates deviation without knowledge, unlike knowingly doing wrong.", "reasons": "Ibn Atiyya contrasts mukhtiʾ and khāṭiʾ, with usage examples and 69:37."}, {"id": "33:5/q18/p2", "position": "Its hamza is pronounced because form IV takes hamzat al-qaṭʿ.", "reasons": "Bursevi states the morphology."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q19", "question": "What deliberate action is blamed?", "turns_on": "Known false descent, post-prohibition conduct, or intended inheritance status.", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q19/p1", "position": "Knowingly assigning another father incurs blame.", "reasons": "Hasan, Qatada and Tabari stress knowledge; Ibn Kathir compares 2:225; Alusi compares 2:283 on the heart."}, {"id": "33:5/q19/p2", "position": "Deliberate attribution after the revealed prohibition incurs blame.", "reasons": "Mujahid and others distinguish the clarified rule from old practice."}, {"id": "33:5/q19/p3", "position": "Intending to treat an adoptee as a biological heir is the culpable act.", "reasons": "Zajjaj and Abu Ishaq distinguish casual 'son' from legal inheritance intent."}, {"id": "33:5/q19/p4", "position": "Deliberate sins call for repentance while mistakes are excused.", "reasons": "Umar contrasts them; Alusi reports the Prophet fearing deliberate wrong rather than forgetfulness."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q20", "question": "How is the second mā parsed?", "turns_on": "Genitive coordination versus nominative subject with an omitted predicate.", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q20/p1", "position": "It is genitive, coordinated with mā in fīmā.", "reasons": "Farra and Tabari supply the construction; Alusi answers the objection about separation from a genitive governor by coordinating each relative with its clause."}, {"id": "33:5/q20/p2", "position": "It is a nominative subject with an omitted predicate assigning liability to intention.", "reasons": "Nahhas, Qurtubi, Samin, Razi, Baydawi, Bursevi and Alusi recover liability from context."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q21", "question": "What warning attaches to knowingly claiming false descent?", "turns_on": "The reports express exclusion from Paradise, curse, or kufr.", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q21/p1", "position": "Paradise is barred to one who knowingly claims another father.", "reasons": "Saʿd and Abu Bakra transmit the Prophetic warning; Qurtubi names the Sahih collections and Alusi notes major-sin classification."}, {"id": "33:5/q21/p2", "position": "Claiming another father or patron brings God's, angels' and people's curse and rejection of deeds.", "reasons": "Thaʿlabi, Tabarsi, Alusi and Ibn Ashur transmit variants; Ibn Ashur includes ransom."}, {"id": "33:5/q21/p3", "position": "Knowingly claiming or disowning false lineage is called disbelief.", "reasons": "Qurtubi cites Abu Dharr; Ibn Kathir mentions an abrogated wording and slander of lineage; Alusi grades the Amr ibn Shuayb report hasan."}, {"id": "33:5/q21/p4", "position": "False attribution is forbidden and deliberate naming contrary to the known father is sinful.", "reasons": "Tabarsi cites Sunnah warnings; Ibn Ashur derives prohibition from the imperative; Qurtubi specifically forbids deliberate 'Zayd ibn Muhammad'."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q22", "question": "May nonliteral family terms or old adoptive names still be used?", "turns_on": "The scope of the prohibition and the risk of lineage confusion.", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q22/p1", "position": "Affectionate 'my son' or respectful 'my father' is permitted absent a lineage claim.", "reasons": "Razi and Alusi distinguish affection from pagan adoption. Ibn Ashur distinguishes grandchildren, nonadopted children, and clear honorifics, citing the Prophet's use, poetry, and the later Farewell Pilgrimage address."}, {"id": "33:5/q22/p2", "position": "Such address is discouraged when it creates suspicion or imitates unbelievers.", "reasons": "Ibn Ashur cautions against casual use. Al-Khafaji and a report of Ibn Hajar call it disliked; Alusi prefers an imitation rationale while rejecting its fit to this verse's direct ban."}, {"id": "33:5/q22/p3", "position": "Old adoptive names sometimes persisted, but deliberate false naming of Zayd is sinful.", "reasons": "Qurtubi cites al-Miqdad and Salim; Ibn Ashur objects that continued use cannot prove intent."}]}

{"id": "33:5/q24", "question": "Why name the heart as agent of intention?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q24/p1", "position": "Assigning intent to hearts is familiar Quranic wording.", "reasons": "Alusi compares 2:283; Biqai reads the feminine verb as hinting at feminine softness and the abundant plural as widening deliberate guilt."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q25", "question": "What do divine forgiveness and mercy address?", "turns_on": "Earlier custom, innocent error, and repentance.", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q25/p1", "position": "They forgive earlier adoptive speech and conduct.", "reasons": "Muqatil names 'Zayd son of Muhammad'; Mawardi adds pre-Islamic ignorance and repentance; Ibn Atiyya says the attributes also apply generally."}, {"id": "33:5/q25/p2", "position": "God lifts blame from mistakes and forgives deliberate sinners who repent.", "reasons": "Qurtubi, Nasafi, Abu Hayyan, Biqai, Alusi and Ibn Ashur distribute the attributes across error and repentance. Bursevi adds negligent causes of error and Umar's call to seek forgiveness for sins."}, {"id": "33:5/q25/p3", "position": "Forgiveness covers the subordinate's wrong; mercy helps the helpless; their order reflects covering then provision.", "reasons": "Razi excludes fearful concealment and self-interested kindness; he describes the converse order as favor then withheld punishment."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q26", "question": "What happened to Salim after adoption ended, and how was nursing understood?", "turns_on": "General precedent versus a special dispensation.", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q26/p1", "position": "The Prophet told Sahla to nurse adult Salim five times, establishing milk kinship.", "reasons": "Aisha and Urwa report that his earlier adoptive status had allowed entry to Abu Hudhayfa's household."}, {"id": "33:5/q26/p2", "position": "Aisha applied the instruction to other men she wished to admit.", "reasons": "Ibn Hibban and Malik say her sister and nieces nursed them."}, {"id": "33:5/q26/p3", "position": "The other wives regarded the instruction as a concession for Salim alone.", "reasons": "They refused to admit others on this basis."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q27", "question": "What examples illuminate unknown fathers or corrected affiliation?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q27/p1", "position": "Abu Bakra said his father was unknown, so he was a religious brother or ally.", "reasons": "The donkey remark varies between his father and narrator; Qurtubi says hadith transmitters name him Nufay ibn al-Harith; Thaʿlabi's variant names Abu Bakr."}, {"id": "33:5/q27/p2", "position": "Salim's father was unknown and he was Abu Hudhayfa's client.", "reasons": "Durr cites Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd that he was only their ally."}, {"id": "33:5/q27/p3", "position": "The Prophet called Zayd their brother and client in the custody dispute over Hamza's daughter.", "reasons": "Ali, Zayd and Jaʿfar competed; the Prophet awarded the girl to her maternal aunt Asma bint Umays."}]}

{"id": "33:5/q29", "question": "How does this verse connect with nearby statements?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q29/p1", "position": "The one-heart and zihar examples in 33:4 prepare the correction of fictive sonship.", "reasons": "Ibn Kathir cites 58:3; Kuranyolu treats one heart as grounding the impossibility of two biological fathers and criticism of pagan customs; Biqai connects later events."}, {"id": "33:5/q29/p2", "position": "The command elaborates God's truth and straight path.", "reasons": "Al-Tibi reads the preceding declaration through this command and the sura's end; Ibn Ashur says the reason reassures hearers of 33:4."}, {"id": "33:5/q29/p3", "position": "Clause connection and separation signal emphasis, resumption and contrast.", "reasons": "Nasafi notes the imperative, declarative, nominal, imperative pattern; Al-Tibi discusses through 33:6."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q30", "question": "How does the no-blame clause relate to the command?", "turns_on": "Parenthetical conclusion versus a proposed implicit command.", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q30/p1", "position": "It reassures and adds a ruling while reinforcing obedience.", "reasons": "Alusi calls it parenthetical; Biqai says fī makes error wholly free of sin, unlike a wording that might suggest partial sin."}, {"id": "33:5/q30/p2", "position": "It implies a command against deliberately calling adoptees children.", "reasons": "Alusi reports but rejects this as strained."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q31", "question": "What is enduring spiritual lineage?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q31/p1", "position": "Connection to the Prophet through poverty, prophethood and Sunnah endures.", "reasons": "Bursevi cites a hadith that all lineage and nobility end except the Prophet's and says figurative family ties may be broken if they lead to sin, citing 31:15."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q32", "question": "How does paternal lineage compare with words shared across languages?", "turns_on": "Exclusive ancestry versus possible shared language.", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q32/p1", "position": "Biological lineage is exclusive, while the same word can belong to multiple languages.", "reasons": "Tabari compares a region both plain and mountain or land and sea."}, {"id": "33:5/q32/p2", "position": "Some Quranic words are exclusively foreign or borrowed.", "reasons": "Tabari rejects this because God calls the Quran Arabic; reverse borrowing is equally possible absent proof."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q33", "question": "What plural forms does fatā have?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q33/p1", "position": "Fityān and fitya.", "reasons": "Majaz records these forms."}]}
{"id": "33:5/q34", "question": "What other warnings appear in the lineage discussion?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "33:5/q34/p1", "position": "The Prophet warned against exalting him as Christians exalted Jesus.", "reasons": "Ibn Kathir cites Umar's report: call him God's servant and messenger."}, {"id": "33:5/q34/p2", "position": "Umar reported the stoning verse and practice.", "reasons": "Ibn Kathir adduces this beside an abrogated wording on fathers."}]}
{"id": "33:43/q01", "question": "How does this verse answer the preceding commands to remember and glorify God?", "turns_on": "The notes give different links to the surrounding passage.", "positions": [{"id": "33:43/q01/p1", "position": "God and the angels bless those who remember Him; His response rewards and encourages their remembrance.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Durr say remembrance has no fixed limit and applies in every condition, unlike other duties. Rāzī says divine mercy despite human forgetfulness encourages remembrance. Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀshūr cite 2:152 and the divine report that God remembers the servant in a better assembly. Ibn ʿĀshūr calls the prayer a like but greater reward for morning and evening remembrance. Ṭabāṭabāʾī contrasts 9:67 with 2:152 and identifies remembrance with mercy and light. Kashshāf and Nasafī connect mercy with God's commands to remembrance, prayer, obedience and good."}, {"id": "33:43/q01/p2", "position": "The passage turns from the believers' promised victory to address and honor the Prophet as their leader.", "reasons": "Al-Biqāʿī relates the turn to the preceding admonition and promised victory."}]}
{"id": "33:43/q02", "question": "Who receives the prayer announced here?", "turns_on": "Whether the occasion restricts the scope of the address.", "positions": [{"id": "33:43/q02/p1", "position": "It was revealed about the Helpers, the Anṣār.", "reasons": "Muqātil says God forgives them and orders angels to ask forgiveness for them."}, {"id": "33:43/q02/p2", "position": "Its mercy extends to all believers, beyond the first hearers.", "reasons": "Rāzī says the closing term believers is glad tidings beyond the original audience. Al-Ālūsī says it affirms mercy to all believers."}]}
{"id": "33:43/q03", "question": "What occasion is reported for the revelation of 33:43?", "turns_on": "The reports differ in setting and in who voiced the question.", "positions": [{"id": "33:43/q03/p1", "position": "After 33:56 announced prayer upon the Prophet, Abū Bakr or the Companions asked whether believers shared that honor, and this verse answered.", "reasons": "The reports vary in speaker: Anas or Mujāhid relate Abū Bakr's remark; Ibn ʿAbbās relates a question by Emigrants and Helpers, and al-Wāḥidī mentions their congratulations. Kashshāf says the consequent wording was 'their greeting'; Muqātil calls this the revealed answer. All link the answer to the honor announced in 33:56."}, {"id": "33:43/q03/p2", "position": "One Miʿrāj account says the verse through 'merciful' was revealed directly to the Prophet at the two-bows distance.", "reasons": "Bursevī's account says God told Muḥammad to wait because his Lord was praying; Muḥammad objected that God needs no prayer, and God answered that His mercy preceded anger. It says Gabriel was absent there."}, {"id": "33:43/q03/p3", "position": "A second Miʿrāj version has Gabriel stop the Prophet in the seventh heaven and say the Lord is praying.", "reasons": "The answer in this version calls God the Holy Lord of angels and Spirit and says His mercy preceded anger."}]}
{"id": "33:43/q04", "question": "What does God's ṣalāt upon believers mean?", "turns_on": "The sources gloss divine ṣalāt by mercy, forgiveness, praise, honor, blessing, public good mention, general care, proximity or inward gifts.", "positions": [{"id": "33:43/q04/p1", "position": "God shows believers mercy, compassion and blessing.", "reasons": "Yaḥyā reports Ibn ʿAbbās; al-Ḥasan's Israelite report says mercy precedes wrath.
